title: Continuity can be checked on a subbase of the target
statement: Let $X$ be a topological space, let $Y$ be a set and let $\mathcal{B}$ be a collection of subsets of $Y$. Give $Y$ the topology generated by $\mathcal{B}$, that is, the coarsest topology on $Y$ in which every member of $\mathcal{B}$ is open (its open sets are the unions of finite intersections of members of $\mathcal{B}$, the empty intersection being $Y$), so that $\mathcal{B}$ is a subbase of it. Then a map $f:X\to Y$ is continuous if and only if $f^{-1}(B)$ is open in $X$ for every $B\in\mathcal{B}$.
